title: Temozolomide Rechallenge in Glioblastoma: A Retrospective Cohort Study
summary: Glioblastoma is the most common malignant brain tumor in adults. Almost all patients experience a relapse after initial treatment. For tumors with a specific feature (MGMT methylation), two chemotherapy options are commonly used at first relapse: another course of temozolomide or a combination of lomustine and etoposide. It is still unclear which works better. We therefore analyze existing treatment data from the Department of Neurology in Heidelberg and compare how long patients lived without disease progression, and overall, after each therapy. Patients are not burdened in any way.

interventions.name: TMZ rechallenge: Patients with MGMT promoter-hypermethylated glioblastoma (CNS WHO grade 4, IDH wild-type). criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Histologically confirmed glioblastoma (CNS WHO grade 4, IDH wild-type)
Confirmed MGMT promoter hypermethylation
Age ≥ 18 years at initial diagnosis
Initial tumor resection
TMZ-based first-line therapy (Stupp or CeTeG regimen)
Documented first recurrence treated with systemic TMZ rechallenge or CCNU/VP16
Treated at the Department of Neurology, Heidelberg, between 01 Jan 2000 and 21 May 2025
Exclusion criteria:
Biopsy only, without resection
Missing or non-standard first-line therapy, in particular no radiochemotherapy
Treatment within an interventional trial that relevantly altered the course of therapy
Systemic therapy at recurrence with a regimen other than TMZ rechallenge or CCNU/VP16
Incomplete documentation of the dates required for the primary endpoints
